title: Republic
author: Plato
short_summary: Plato's dialogue exploring the nature of justice, the ideal city-state, and the philosopher's role in governance.
central_argument: Justice is harmony — each part of the soul and city doing its proper function. Only philosopher-kings, who know the Form of the Good, are fit to rule.

title: Nicomachean Ethics
author: Aristotle
short_summary: Aristotle's systematic account of how humans can live well and achieve happiness through virtuous activity.
central_argument: Happiness (eudaimonia) is not a feeling but an activity — living and functioning well according to virtue over a complete life.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
short_summary: Personal writings of the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius — a private journal of Stoic philosophical practice.
central_argument: We cannot control external events, only our responses. Virtue and reason are the only true goods. Death and change are natural — accept them.

title: Leviathan
author: Thomas Hobbes
short_summary: Hobbes argues that without political authority, human life is war of all against all, requiring a sovereign to maintain peace.
central_argument: In the state of nature life is 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short.' Rational agents agree to a social contract surrendering freedoms to a sovereign for security.

title: Second Treatise of Government
author: John Locke
short_summary: Locke argues that legitimate government derives from the consent of the governed and must protect natural rights.
central_argument: People have natural rights to life, liberty, and property. Government is legitimate only by consent. When it violates rights, revolution is justified.

title: Critique of Pure Reason
author: Immanuel Kant
short_summary: Kant's investigation into the conditions and limits of human knowledge, synthesizing rationalism and empiricism.
central_argument: The mind actively structures experience. Space, time, and categories like causality are frameworks the mind imposes on reality — not features of things-in-themselves.

title: Phenomenology of Spirit
author: G.W.F. Hegel
short_summary: Hegel traces the development of consciousness from simple sense-perception to absolute knowing through dialectical stages.
central_argument: Consciousness develops through contradiction and resolution (thesis-antithesis-synthesis). Spirit (Geist) realizes itself through history and human self-understanding.

title: Thus Spoke Zarathustra
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
short_summary: Through the prophet Zarathustra, Nietzsche proclaims the death of God and calls for a revaluation of all values.
central_argument: With God dead, humanity must create its own values. The Übermensch embraces life, affirms eternal recurrence, and overcomes nihilism through creative will.

title: Being and Time
author: Martin Heidegger
short_summary: Heidegger investigates the meaning of Being through analysis of human existence (Dasein) and our relationship with time.
central_argument: Humans are 'thrown' into existence without choosing it. Authentic existence means owning one's finitude and living toward death rather than fleeing into 'the they'.

title: A Theory of Justice
author: John Rawls
short_summary: Rawls constructs principles of justice that rational agents would choose if they did not know their place in society.
central_argument: Justice is fairness. Behind a veil of ignorance, rational agents choose: equal basic liberties for all, and social inequalities only if they benefit the least advantaged.
